title: The Drowned Tower
subtitle: Fort on the Lake: the island and the first cellars

beats.text: The Fort docks. Captain Maren coils a wet rope and does not smile.

beats.speaker: maren
beats.text: Row to the Isle of Old Stone. Find out who lands there, and what moves in the water.
One boat. One hero. Maren waits to hear who goes.

choices.ask: Who rows to the Isle of Old Stone?

options.label: The Fighter
options.sub: A sword and 8 hit points. Strong at doors.

then.text: You belt on the sword and take the oars.

options.label: The Wizard
options.sub: A dagger, 4 hit points, and one Sleep spell.

then.text: You tuck the dagger in your belt. The word of Sleep waits behind your teeth.

scenes.title: The Broken Jetty
scenes.place: The Isle of Old Stone, sunset

beats.text: Four hours of oars later, the sun is low and the island is close.
A stone jetty runs out from the south shore. Half of it has fallen into the lake.
On a mooring post, a rope burn shows pale and fresh: someone else lands here.
Past the end of the jetty, something large moves under the water, a long shadow, and is gone.

options.label: Walk up to the tower shell

beats.text: A round tower, thirty feet across, open to the sky. Its upper floors fell in long ago and lie as rubble on the ground.
A stair climbs the inside wall to a broken top forty feet up. Crows watch you from the rim with the calm of tax collectors.
The trapdoor lies open in the rubble. A stair goes down into the dark.

choices.ask: What do you look at? Looking is free.

then.text: You shift stones for ten minutes. Under the rubble lies a trapdoor of black oak.
Its iron ring is furred with rust. It lifts with a groan.
From the broken top you see the whole island: rock, pine, the jetty, the cottage.
At the north cliff a boat-shaped shadow lies on the water.

beats.text: A stone cottage beside the tower. The roof is gone.
The hearth holds ash less than a week old.
A tin of lamp oil sits on a shelf, enough for two flasks.
On the door someone has chalked an eye with a line through it. It is not a greeting.

choices.ask: What do you do here? Looking is free.

options.label: Take the tin of lamp oil

then.text: You take the tin. It is heavy, and the oil in it is clean.
The chalk is white and fresh. One eye, wide open. One straight line through it, drawn hard.
Rain has not touched it yet.

beats.text: Under the trapdoor a stone stair goes down twenty feet. The air smells of old oil and wet stone.
At the bottom stands an oak door, swollen in its frame. It is stuck.
The door still holds. Whatever is behind it heard you try it.

then.text: Scratching. Squeaks. Many small feet.

choices.ask: The door is stuck. What do you do?

options.label: Put your shoulder to the door

then.text: The door bursts open with a crack like a dropped plank.
You work oil from the tin into each hinge. Then you push. The door swings open without a sound.
The door shudders and holds. The noise rolls away into the dark.

choices.ask: The door is still shut. Where do you go?

options.label: Climb back up to the tower

beats.text: Racks of broken oil jars. The floor is tacky.
Five giant rats, each the size of a cat, lift their heads from the spill.
The oiled door made no sound.
But they heard you at the door before. All five face the doorway.

choices.ask: One rat leaps. What do you do?

then.text: You hold the doorway. Only two rats can reach you at a time.
Your blow throws the first one back among the jars. Then the second.
The pack breaks. The rest flee down the far stair.
You speak the word of Sleep.
One by one the rats sag into the spill. Their whiskers twitch. They do not wake.
You strike at the first rat. It dodges. Two more come over the jars.
You fall among the broken jars. The rats close in.
You back up the stair. The rats do not follow.

choices.ask: The room is yours. What now?

then.text: In one rack, five flasks of oil are still whole. You take them.

options.label: Go on to the far stair

beats.text: A second stair goes down into black water.
As you watch, the water climbs one step, as if the lake took a breath.
Five flasks of oil clink in your pack. That is light for another day.
The first delve ends here. You row home to tell Maren what moves under the island.
You row back across the dark water. The Fort's lamps come up out of the lake.
Captain Maren meets you at the docks. She does not smile.

beats.speaker: maren
beats.text: The island will still be there tomorrow. So will whoever lands on it.
Your torch rolls away across the oily floor and goes out.
Far above, the crows wait on the tower rim. Captain Maren will send someone else to the island.
